title: Adaptive Progress Checkpointing Optimized for Interruption Risk and Verified Recovery
target_platform: Multi-agent coordination harness; manage_coordination.py; relay.py; evaluating-agent-work telemetry (ceiling 1M tokens, 12 execution-hours)
hypothesis: A checkpoint policy using measured interruption risk, progress value, and checkpoint cost will: (a) produce >= 20% more verified completed subgoals per fixed resource budget than the best fixed-interval policy on development data; (b) lose <= 5% of acknowledged progress; (c) keep checkpoint overhead <= 10% of inference tokens; and (d) lose no more than 3% throughput in interruption-free controls.
falsification_criteria: Fail if any threshold is missed, or if the adaptive policy uses advance knowledge of the held-out interruption schedule.
experiment: Run 30 multi-stage tasks under frozen interruption schedules (context reset, worker termination, simulated quota denial, vendor handoff). Compare fixed-step checkpoints, fixed-time checkpoints, end-only persistence, and the adaptive policy. Score independently verified subgoals, not self-reported completion.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Frontier models are limited to participating in multi-vendor handoff tests under the 1M token ceiling.
